title: Ari's reply blocks
description: A reply is Markdown. Where its content has a shape, Ari writes it as a fenced block whose info string is `ari:` and a kind, holding one JSON object, and the app draws it natively. A block the app doesn't recognise, or whose JSON doesn't parse, shows as its fenced text. Blocks are never spoken on a call.

Place.title: ari:place
Place.description: A place you might go. The app opens it in Maps.

Choices.title: ari:choices
Choices.description: Short answers you might give next, to tap. A tap sends the label as an ordinary message; unlike an ask, nothing waits for it.

Motion.title: ari:motion
Motion.description: A compact line under a reply when Ari starts or changes a thing in motion, such as "Florence trip: booked the Uffizi". Tapping it opens the thing. Draw the line from the `MotionChange` with that version, or from the thing's title when there's none.

change.description: The thing's version the line is about.

Images.title: ari:images
Images.description: Pictures Ari found on the web, kept on the server as attachments so the app never contacts their hosts. Never generated.

source_url.description: The page the picture came from.

credit.description: Who made it, as its source asks.

File.title: ari:file
File.description: A file Ari made or changed for you to look at before it goes anywhere, such as a PDF, at one version. Draw it as a card with its name, kind, size and version that opens a preview (a PDF's pages) and shares it. `GET /v0/files/{file}` gives its versions and their attachments; fetch the bytes, exactly as made, with `GET /v0/attachments/{attachment}`. When a newer version exists, say so on the card. Feedback on a card is about its version.

Proposals.title: ari:proposals
Proposals.description: Changes Ari proposes and hasn't made, such as after reading a recording: each row one change, with Skip and its own verb. Nothing is applied until you tap the verb, and there's no accepting them all. A tapped verb sends your message with an `ari:decision` block, and Ari then makes that change and says so; the row shows its `done` line with Undo, which sends `undo`. Skip stays on your phone and never reaches Ari. Show how many are done, such as "1 of 3 done".

title.description: A heading over them, such as "What I'd change".

id.description: The row's id, unique in the block, which its decision names.

kind.description: What it changes, for its symbol: `calendar`, `draft` (a mail draft, never sent), `memory`, `desk`, `motion`, `wakeup` or `other`. Draw a kind you don't know as `other`.

title.description: The change, such as "Hold Thursday 15:00 for the CTO round".

detail.description: One line on why or how.

verb.description: Its button, a word or two, such as "Add", "Draft it" or "Keep".

done.description: What the row says once accepted, such as "Added to your calendar".

Decision.title: ari:decision
Decision.description: In your message, not Ari's: the row of an `ari:proposals` block you tapped. `accept` asks Ari to make exactly that change now; `undo` to take back what it made for it. The message's first line says the same in words, which is what the chat shows; the app leaves the block out of your bubble.

message.description: Ari's message that holds the block.

Attach.title: ari:attach
Attach.description: In your message, not Ari's: "Use in draft" on a file Ari showed. Ari attaches exactly that version, which waits in its workspace at `shown/<file>/v<version>/<name>`, to the mail draft it's for, and never sends it. The message's first line says the same in words; the app leaves the block out of your bubble.
